state.case_summary:
A woman in her 80s presented with a 1-week history of progressive, painful blisters and ulcers of the groin. She reported enlargement of the tongue over the past 3 months, leading to difficulty with mastication. She also experienced numbness without weakness of her distal lower limbs for 3 months, which restricted her mobility requiring diapers. Her medical history included IgG λ-type multiple myeloma complicated by anemia and lytic lesions in the calvarium, managed conservatively with transfusions. She was taking folic acid and intramuscular cyanocobalamin supplements due to deficiencies attributed to dietary cause.

Circinate purpuric patches with erosions on the natal cleft, buttocks, inguinal creases, and vulva. Hemorrhagic flaccid bullae on the posterior perineum. Macroglossia, glossitis, and a hemorrhagic erosion on the hard palate. Purpuric macules present periorbitally, on the lips, inframammary folds, forearms, and thighs.

- Laboratory findings:
  * Platelet count: 171 × 103/μL (reference range, 140-440 × 103/μL)
  * Prothrombin time: 11.7 seconds (reference range, 9.9-11.4 seconds)
  * Activated partial thromboplastin time: 36.0 seconds (reference range, 25.7-32.9 seconds)
  * Serum zinc: 34.4 μg/dL (reference range, 72.4-124.4 μg/dL)

- Biopsy findings:
  * Initial punch biopsies from right inframammary fold and perineal blister were inconclusive
  * Repeated biopsy from left groin showed subepidermal blister lined by fibrin and chronic inflammatory infiltrate, with scattered short eosinophilic bands in the dermis showing apple-green birefringence on polarized light microscopy with Congo red staining
  * Direct immunofluorescence test was negative

- Additional tests:
  * Herpes simplex virus PCR from perineal ulcer swab was negative
